## Welcome to WISE-APP docs

**WISE-APP** (Weather Impact Simulation and Evaluation for Adaptation Policy and Planning) is a tool designed to estimate potential welfare outcomes under different weather conditions before events occur. 

It quantifies the relationship between weather and welfare, simulates outcomes under historical and future climate scenarios, and evaluates the impact of various adaptation policies.

This user guide walks you through all key features and steps to use WISE-APP effectively.

## How to access WISE-APP

[WISE-APP online](https://datanalytics-int.worldbank.org/content/5163b09e-1eb3-47e6-bb6a-4f0abcf7a28f) *DEV version*

- This option requires World Bank single sign-on credentials. 



[WISE-APP R package](https://github.com/worldbank/welfare-weather-app) *DEV version*

- This option requires R and access to WISE-APP data.
- To install and run locally:


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
remotes::install_github("worldbank/welfare-weather-app")
wiseapp::run_app()
```
:::


## This guide

This guide includes the following sections:

- **Data** — An overview of the household survey and weather data that underpin WISE-APP, including sources, structure, and coverage.
- **Model Welfare** — Decisions, defaults, and interpretation guidance for the modelling step.
- **Simulate Welfare** — How to configure and run historical and climate-scenario simulations, and how to read the results.
- **Policy Scenarios** — How to define and interpret each type of policy intervention.

## Data

WISE-APP connects to a data directory containing household survey microdata and weather data. The data are spatially linked using the H3 indexing system. For more details on the data sources, structure, aand coverage, see the [Data section](data.qmd) of this guide.

- [This repository](https://github.com/worldbank/welfare-weather-app-data) contains the code used to prepare specific data sources for WISE-APP.

## Analysis

After connecting to the data, WISE-APP performs analysis in 3 steps:

- **Model Welfare** — Establish the statistical relationship between weather and outcomes of interest. The fitted model is the foundation for all subsequent steps.
- **Simulate Welfare** — Apply the fitted model to historical and future climate scenarios to produce a distribution of weather-driven outcomes.
- **Policy Scenarios** — Re-simulate outcomes under counterfactual policy interventions (social protection, infrastructure, digital access, labour market) to quantify direct welfare gains and changes in climate resilience.
